prerequisites: Basic knowledge of algebra, geometry, and mathematical analysis (including trigonometry, algebraic equations, function analysis, and introductory concepts of differential and integral calculus).
Knowledge of Methods for Technical Representation
Physical, technological, and mechanical properties of metallic materials
Elements of physics, mathematical analysis, physics and mechanics

learning_outcomes.text: Give the students the knowledge of the principal manufacturing techniques, focusing on the main conventional material-processing methods (Foundry, Machining, Plastic Deformation, and Welding).

Enable students to develop a basic understanding of the technical challenges inherent to production processes and to identify and structure the technological procedures most suitable for manufacturing a given component.
Introduce simplified yet effective methodological approaches for performing, selecting, and determining the data required for the design of Foundry, Machining, and Plastic Deformation processes.
Use tables and charts for selecting tools and process parameters.
Determine the appropriate machine tool dimensions for Machining and Plastic Deformation operations.
Prepare and interpret a process sheet.
Critically compare different technological solutions and identify the most appropriate one.
Acquire and employ the terminology specific to manufacturing processes.
Integrate diverse learning resources (textbooks, including those in English, online videos, and technical catalogues).

The student identifies and describes the main manufacturing processes used in the production of industrial components, along with their related physical principles, machinery, tools, technological parameters, fields of application, advantages, and limitations.

The student analyzes a component and selects the appropriate manufacturing processes; he designs the manufacturing cycle, identifying operational sequences, tools, equipment, machines, and process parameters consistent with the geometric and functional requirements.

The student can critically compare alternative technological solutions, evaluating achievable quality, productivity, costs, process limitations, defects, and the sustainability of production choices in accordance with the technical specifications provided.

The student explains how the processes work using correct technical and scientific language, justifies technological choices, clearly discusses parameters, equipment, tools, and expected results, and develops manufacturing cycles suitable for production.
The student uses independent study methods to gain a deeper understanding of traditional and advanced manufacturing processes, consulting technical texts, handouts, and industrial documentation.

syllabus_topics: Foundry Techniques: Study of solidification and cooling of castings; cooling modulus; shrinkage phenomena; residual stresses. Design of the pattern, gating system, and feeding system. Techniques for the production of expendable moulds (sand moulding). Main characteristics of permanent mould casting. Typical casting defects.

Plastic Deformation Processes: Mechanisms of hot and cold plastic deformation. Bulk deformation processes (Forging, Rolling, Extrusion, Drawing). Calculation of forces and power requirements. Introduction to sheet-metal forming processes.

Machining Processes: Fundamentals of cutting processes: orthogonal cutting; mechanics of chip formation and shear-plane models; cutting forces. Cutting tools and tool geometry; rake and and clearance angles in turning tools. Tool wear mechanisms; optimization of machining operations. Process parameters and main characteristics of the conventional machining techniques (Turning, Milling, Drilling) and related machine tools. Process planning and machining cycles.
Overview of Main Conventional Welding Techniques: Characteristics and applications of the principal conventional welding processes.
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as the arithmetic mean of the Practical and Theoretical test scores, rounded up to the nearest whole number. Students are admitted to the theoretical test only after passing the practical test with a minimum score of 16/30. For the Practical Test, students must demonstrate at least the ability to set up a conceptually correct solution procedure for each exercise, and it is not permitted to leave any exercise completely unanswered. For the Theoretical Test, students must show adequate command of the subject matter and appropriate technical vocabulary, as well as a sufficient ability to independently elaborate the required concepts, including through the use of schemes and diagrams where appropriate; a complete lack of knowledge of any proposed topics is not acceptable. The final grade is expressed on a 30-point scale.
